title: removeWords
summary: Remove selected words from tokenized documents or bag-of-words models.

gpu_support.notes: `removeWords` filters host text-model objects and does not use provider kernels.

description: `removeWords(documents, words)` removes selected tokens from RunMat `tokenizedDocument` compatibility objects. `removeWords(bag, words)` removes matching vocabulary columns from RunMat `bagOfWords` objects. `words` can also be numeric 1-based vocabulary indices or a logical mask the same length as the object's vocabulary.
behaviors: `documents` must be a RunMat `tokenizedDocument` object created by `tokenizedDocument`.
`bag` must be a RunMat `bagOfWords` object created by `bagOfWords`.
`words` can be a string vector, character vector, or cell array of character vectors. A character vector is treated as one word.
`idx` can be a numeric vector of positive integer vocabulary positions or a logical array whose length matches the object's `Vocabulary`.
`removeWords(___, 'IgnoreCase', true)` removes string-selected or index-selected vocabulary words without case sensitivity. The default is case-sensitive.
For tokenized documents, the result preserves `Shape`, `TokenizeMethod`, and `Language` metadata while recomputing document lengths and vocabulary.
For bag-of-words models, the result preserves document row count and removes matching count columns.

examples.input:
documents = tokenizedDocument(["an example of a short sentence"; "a second short sentence"]);
newDocuments = removeWords(documents, ["short" "second"])
examples.output: `newDocuments` contains `an example of a sentence` and `a sentence`.

examples.input:
documents = tokenizedDocument(["I love MATLAB"; "I love MathWorks"]);
newDocuments = removeWords(documents, [1 3])
examples.output: `newDocuments` removes the first and third vocabulary entries.
`newBag` removes count columns for the selected vocabulary words.

faqs.question: Is `removeWords` case-sensitive?
faqs.answer: Yes by default. Use `removeWords(___, 'IgnoreCase', true)` for case-insensitive matching.

faqs.question: Does a logical index mask need to match the vocabulary length?
faqs.answer: Yes. RunMat rejects logical masks whose length differs from the object's vocabulary length.

faqs.question: Does `removeWords` execute on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. It filters host text/model metadata and has no `runmat-accelerate` provider path.

example.input:
newDocuments = removeWords(documents, words)
newBag = removeWords(bag, words)
newDocuments = removeWords(___, 'IgnoreCase', true)
newDocuments = removeWords(documents, idx)
newBag = removeWords(bag, idx)
example.output: `newDocuments` is a `tokenizedDocument` compatibility object. `newBag` is a `bagOfWords` compatibility object.

points: Input objects must be RunMat Text Analytics compatibility objects from this module.
Numeric indices are 1-based positive integers into the object's vocabulary.
Logical masks must have the same number of elements as the object's vocabulary.

gpu_residency: `removeWords` filters host text/model objects and has no provider kernel.
